results.title: Funded Research - Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative
results.content: Recently, Wharton AI and Analytics Initiative funded a project to study “Reducing Gender and Racial Disparities in the Use of Generative AI in the Workplace.” While this research intends to enhance both academic research and practice over the longer-term, there is an immediate need to ensure that the “digital divide” in AI adoption does not manifest (or widen) among students enrolled in the courses, MGMT 2240 and MGMT 6240, Leading Diversity in Organizations. This research project aims to investigate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) investments by non-tech firms (AI-adopters) on product market competition, innovation, and industry dynamics. With proprietary data from Upwork Inc., the researchers are able to access full information on a large sample of jobs and workers over time, thus obtaining findings that can inform the effects of generative AI on the labor market and careers.

results.title: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) for Sustainable Tourism
results.content: Positioning, navigation, and alert services for accurate geolocation and safety; [3] Enabling smart and adaptive tourism through dynamic route optimization and behavioral mapping; [4] Integration with IoT, GIS, and AI for real-time data collection and predictive analytics; and [5] Managing visitor demand and environmental impact via traffic regulation, resource monitoring, and carrying capacity assessments. GNSS technologies support sustainable tourism by enabling navigation, smart visitor management, integration with digital tools, and monitoring of environmental impact. To support operational tourism planning, GNSS-R data can be integrated into digital dashboards and mobile systems that deliver context-aware, real-time recommendations to both managers and visitors. Fifth, there is significant potential in developing open-access digital platforms that combine GNSS data with sustainability performance dashboards, such as the Smart City Dashboard of Amsterdam, which integrates mobility and environmental data for urban planning, or the VISIT Greenland Portal, which uses GNSS and sensor data to monitor tourist flows and environmental pressures in protected areas.
